stories.title: Kalamazoo weighs year-long freeze on new data centers
stories.dek: City leaders will debate a moratorium at their next meeting that would block proposals while officials study power and water demands. Residents 30 miles away could see higher electric rates if large projects move forward unchecked. The pause would give local officials time to write rules before any campus breaks ground.
stories.source_title: Kalamazoo city leaders to consider data center moratorium at next meeting - WOODTV.com

stories.title: U.P. locals team with comedian to block AI data centers
stories.dek: Residents in Michigan's Upper Peninsula are pushing back against proposed AI data centers that could strain local power grids and water supplies. Comedian Charlie Berens is amplifying their concerns in public opposition efforts. The fight highlights growing pushback in rural Michigan communities over energy demands from big tech projects.
stories.source_title: Midwestern comedian Charlie Berens joins U.P. residents to oppose A.I. data centers - myupnow.com

stories.title: Marshall blocks new data centers for a full year
stories.dek: The city council approved a moratorium that halts all data-center proposals for at least 12 months. Local residents worried about power demand and noise now have breathing room while planners study impacts. The delay pushes back any large-scale projects that could have drawn hundreds of megawatts from the regional grid.
stories.source_title: Marshall data center moratorium delays development by at least one year - WWMT

stories.title: Developer fights suburb's freeze on power-hungry server farms in court battle
stories.dek: A developer has filed suit against an Oakland County community after it imposed a temporary halt on new data center projects. The case will test how far local governments can go in pausing large-scale facilities that demand hundreds of megawatts and new grid upgrades. Residents 30 miles away could see higher electric rates or altered tax bases depending on the outcome.
stories.source_title: Data center developer sues Oakland County suburb over moratorium - crainsdetroit.com

stories.title: Nessel appeals DTE deal to supply power to Saline data center
stories.dek: Michigan Attorney General Dana Nessel and environmental groups filed opening arguments challenging the contract that would let DTE serve a large data center in Saline. The appeal centers on whether the utility’s rate structure fairly allocates costs for the massive new load. Local residents could see higher electric bills if the contract stands as written.
stories.source_title: Nessel and environmental groups file initial arguments in appeal of DTE Saline data center contract - News From The States

stories.title: Michigan data centers hit new tax and power fights this week
stories.dek: The weekly Michigan Advance roundup tracks active fights over tax breaks, grid upgrades and water use in several townships. Readers 30 miles from any site feel the direct hit on electric bills and local budgets when big projects win incentives. The report pulls together filings and votes that affect ratepayers statewide.
stories.source_title: Michigan Data Centers: The Weekly Download - Michigan Advance

stories.title: Lowell Twp drafts rules to tame data center growth
stories.dek: The planning commission will put forward a new ordinance aimed at data centers. Residents in Kent County and nearby townships could see limits on size, noise and power use if the rules pass. Local officials want to avoid the heavy electricity and water demands that have sparked fights elsewhere in Michigan.
stories.source_title: Lowell Township planning commission set to propose data center ordinance - Yahoo

stories.title: Nessel pushes PSC to block data center cost shifts to ratepayers
stories.dek: Attorney General Dana Nessel called on the Public Service Commission to stop utilities from passing data center infrastructure costs to regular customers. The move targets large power deals that could raise monthly bills across Michigan. Nessel said the commission must protect residents from hidden subsidies for big tech projects.
stories.source_title: Nessel wants to hold PSC 'accountable' in fight against data center - AOL.com

stories.title: West Michigan township gets first look at data center noise, power and water rules
stories.dek: Local officials heard details on how large server farms could affect roads, electric demand and noise levels in their community. Residents 30 miles away could see higher utility rates or new zoning limits if similar projects spread. The presentation focused on drafting local ordinances before any applications arrive.
stories.source_title: Data center presentation explores impacts, ordinances - Shoreline Media Group

stories.title: Michigan senator flags power and water risks from incoming data centers
stories.dek: A state senator is alerting local officials that new data centers could drive up electricity rates and strain water supplies in Michigan suburbs. Communities without strong local rules may end up subsidizing the facilities through higher utility bills. The warning targets growing interest in data-center sites across metro Detroit and surrounding counties.
stories.source_title: State senator warns communities about data centers - C&G Newspapers

stories.title: Ypsilanti Data Center Plan Spotlights Water and Power Tradeoffs
stories.dek: EMU hydrogeologist Christopher Gellasch said closed-loop cooling can reuse groundwater without warming the subsurface, while activist Peter Sinclair noted possible new energy infrastructure as a community benefit.

national.title: Data centers advance rapidly as regulators scramble for rules
national.dek: Across the U.S., officials race to impose guardrails on power-hungry facilities while communities push back on incentives and impacts.
